title: The Button Nobody Could Reach
title_ja: 誰もが押せるわけではなかったボタン
fact_notes: 登場人物・出来事・観察結果は架空の教材例。実測値・実在資料を主張しない。リンクは制作台帳であり外部の実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A group of students designed an electronic question box for visitors at their school festival.
sentences.ja: 生徒グループは学校祭の来場者向けに電子質問箱を設計した。

sentences.en: Visitors could press a button on a screen to choose a topic and receive a short explanation.
sentences.ja: 来場者は画面のボタンを押して話題を選び、短い説明を受け取ることができた。

sentences.en: The designers spent several afternoons checking that every button opened the correct page.
sentences.ja: 設計者は数日間の午後を使い、全ボタンが正しいページを開くか確認した。

sentences.en: They believed that their system was ready because the software operated without any obvious errors.
sentences.ja: 明らかなエラーなくソフトウェアが動作したため、準備が整ったと思った。

sentences.en: On the morning of the festival, the students placed the screen on a high table beside the entrance.
sentences.ja: 学校祭の朝、生徒たちは入口脇の高い机に画面を置いた。

sentences.en: However, a young visitor could not reach the button at the top of the display.
sentences.ja: しかし、小さな来場者は画面上部のボタンに手が届かなかった。

sentences.en: Another visitor found the pale text difficult to read in bright sunlight.
sentences.ja: 別の来場者は明るい日光の中で薄い色の文字が読みにくいと感じた。

sentences.en: These problems had not appeared when the designers tested the system in their usual classroom.
sentences.ja: 設計者がいつもの教室で検証した際にはこれらの問題は現れなかった。

sentences.en: Instead of simply offering to operate the screen for every visitor, the students decided to improve its design.
sentences.ja: 来場者全員の代わりに画面を操作するだけでなく、生徒たちは設計を改善することにした。

sentences.en: They moved the display to a lower table and increased the contrast between the text and its background.
sentences.ja: 画面を低い机に移し、文字と背景のコントラストを高めた。

sentences.en: They also added a large home button in a consistent position on every page.
sentences.ja: 全ページの同じ位置に大きなホームボタンも追加した。

sentences.en: Several visitors then tried the revised version while the designers observed without interrupting them.
sentences.ja: 数人の来場者が修正版を試し、設計者は邪魔せず観察した。

sentences.en: The students discovered that some users still needed additional time to understand the different topic labels.
sentences.ja: 一部の利用者は話題のラベルの違いを理解するのにまだ時間が必要だと分かった。

sentences.en: They replaced several unfamiliar expressions with simpler alternatives and tested the changes again.
sentences.ja: なじみの薄い表現をいくつか簡単なものに置き換え、再度変更を検証した。

sentences.en: Although the revised system was not suitable for every possible visitor, it was easier for more people to use independently.
sentences.ja: 修正版はあり得るすべての来場者に適したわけではないが、より多くの人が自力で使いやすくなった。

sentences.en: The designers recorded the remaining difficulties as possible improvements for their next project.
sentences.ja: 設計者は残る困難を次の活動の改善候補として記録した。

sentences.en: The festival taught the team to distinguish correct operation from successful communication.
sentences.ja: 学校祭を通じ、チームは正しい動作と伝達の成功を区別することを学んだ。

sentences.en: A screen may function perfectly while its intended audience encounters practical barriers.
sentences.ja: 画面が完璧に動作しても、想定利用者が実際の障壁に直面することがある。

sentences.en: For the students, testing technology became a process of learning about the people who would use it.
sentences.ja: 生徒にとって技術の検証はそれを使う人々について学ぶ過程となった。

sentences.en: Their most important discovery was that a working button is not useful unless people can actually use it.
sentences.ja: 最も重要な発見は動くボタンも人が実際に使えなければ役立たないことだった。

vocabulary.definition: people who plan how things work
remaining the same in relevant ways
more than what is already present
put something new in place of another
other things that can be chosen
left after other things have changed
things that are hard to deal with
people for whom information is intended
things making progress or access difficult

questions.prompt: What was the electronic box designed to do?
options: Give visitors short explanations about chosen topics.
Turn off all lights in the building.
questions.explanation_ja: 話題を選ぶと説明を表示する装置。

questions.prompt: Why did the designers first think it was ready?
options: They had interviewed all festival visitors.
The table had been lowered already.
The software appeared to work without errors.
Every visitor had tested it outdoors.
questions.explanation_ja: エラーなく動作したため。

questions.prompt: What difficulty did a young visitor experience?
options: The screen collected too much money.
The top button was out of reach.
questions.explanation_ja: 上部のボタンに手が届かなかった。

questions.prompt: Why did another visitor struggle to read the text?
options: The labels were written upside down.
The text was pale in bright sunlight.
questions.explanation_ja: 日光の下で色が薄く読みにくかった。

questions.prompt: How did the team improve physical access?
options: It placed the screen on a higher shelf.
It moved the screen onto a lower table.

questions.prompt: Why was the home button placed consistently?
options: Users could find it in the same place on every page.
It would change the festival date.
It would remove every topic from the screen.
Only designers needed to locate it.
questions.explanation_ja: 同じ位置なら見つけやすい。

questions.prompt: What did the students change about the labels?
options: They translated all text into an invented language.
They removed the topic choices permanently.
They replaced unfamiliar expressions with simpler ones.
questions.explanation_ja: 難しい表現を簡単なものに変更。

options: At the same time as everyone.

questions.prompt: Why did they record remaining difficulties?
options: To prove their device had no limitations.
To prevent anyone from using the system.
To replace their visitors with designers.
questions.explanation_ja: 次の改善に生かすため。

options: Software errors are the only design problems that matter.
All visitors should ask designers to press buttons.
A working system must also be usable by its intended users.
Testing in one classroom guarantees accessibility.
questions.explanation_ja: 正常動作と利用しやすさは別である。

grammar.focus: when the designers tested the system
grammar.explanation_ja: when節は問題が出なかった時点。

grammar.focus: unless people can actually use it
grammar.explanation_ja: unlessは〜でない限りという条件。

discourse.role_ja: 動作確認済みでも利用上の問題が出たこと。
改善と残る限界を対比する。
正しい機械動作と利用者の問題を対比。

paraphrases.source: They believed that their system was ready because the software operated without any obvious errors.
paraphrases.rewrite: The team thought the device was ready since no clear software faults appeared.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: エラーが見当たらず完成と判断。

paraphrases.source: These problems had not appeared when the designers tested the system in their usual classroom.
paraphrases.rewrite: Their normal classroom tests had not revealed these problems.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 教室では問題が見つからなかった。

paraphrases.source: Several visitors then tried the revised version while the designers observed without interrupting them.
paraphrases.rewrite: Visitors used the updated system as the team quietly watched.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 利用者が試す様子を観察。

paraphrases.source: Their most important discovery was that a working button is not useful unless people can actually use it.
paraphrases.rewrite: Even a functional button is valuable only if people can use it.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 使えることが有用性の条件。

cloze.explanation_ja: 上部のボタンに届かなかった。
文字と背景の違いを大きくした。
なじみのない語を変更。
利用者に障壁があり得る。
